terms.gloss: marsh mallow; used here of the hibiscus
evidence: Verg. E. 10.71: gracilī fiscellam texit hibiscō
terms.comment: Classically the marsh mallow, a plant of the same family, whose slender stems Vergil’s shepherd weaves into a basket. The botanists gave the name to the genus of the hibiscus; its use for the tropical flower is modern, and ours.

terms.gloss: the hibiscus of Asian gardens (the botanical name)

phrases.latin: Vīn' flōrem hibiscī post aurem gerere?
phrases.english: Do you want to wear a hibiscus flower behind your ear?

phrases.latin: Flōs hibiscī ūnum tantum diem flōret.
phrases.english: A hibiscus flower blooms for only one day.

phrases.latin: dum sedet et gracilī fiscellam texit hibiscō
phrases.english: while he sits and weaves a little basket of slender mallow
